key_note: The published star keys are corrupted the same way in Figs 1, 4 and 5 (Figs 1/5: '*p < .05, ****p < .01, *p < .0001'; Fig 4: '*p < .05, ****p < .001, *p < .0001'). '*' gets two thresholds, and the middle symbol each figure actually uses (** in Figs 1/5, *** in Fig 4) is never defined. So the intended keys are evidently */**(***)/**** = <.05/<.01(<.001)/<.0001, matching the paper's own clean Fig 3 key ('*p < .05; ****p < .0001'). An inequality can be taken only for the four-star mark, because its literal printed bound (<.01 or <.001) is weaker than the reconstructed <.0001: it is true under either reading and is the legend's own printed text. '**' and '***' have no printed key entry, so they give nothing.
